#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"

## PR Description

Closes #1137

## Problem

A dev/rework agent that provisions its Dart SDK independently of the target repo ends up with an SDK that differs from the one the repo's CI pins. Dart's formatter and analyzer are version-sensitive: the agent then re-flows hundreds of files CI considers clean, calls CI's 3 changed files "clean", and — worst of all — **disputes a mechanical `dart_format` red**, loop-escalating over a fix that is purely mechanical. A mismatched SDK also poisons analyzer-based claims and any "format-clean" self-verification in the leg summary.

This is a **generic factory property, not a property of any one consumer repo**: every deployment whose runners build Dart projects needs the agent's toolchain to match the repo's CI pin.

### What changed
- `setup/dart.sh` precedence (gh-1137): explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; repos without `pubspec.yaml` skip the install entirely.
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)`; the append is a no-op on failure, non-Dart repos, and when the line is already present.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`).

### Review round 1 (fa-specific must not live in this repo) — to address in the rework leg

The dev/rework **runner configs** are per-deployment artifacts and belong in the consuming repo (or a deployment override), not committed here:

- `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json`, `.dmtools/runners/fa-rework.json` (added in this PR) — move out of dmtools-agents; the runner preamble should be generic: any Dart repo's runner opts into `bash setup/dart.sh` via its own config.
- The two UTs asserting the fa runner configs by name (`fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json customParams.setupCommands`) — replace with generic contracts: e.g. "if a runner config declares a dart preamble, it runs setup/dart.sh" + the setup/summary scripts' own unit tests (already 54+14 cases).
- The `setup/dart.sh` header comment referencing the fa dev/rework runner — reword to "the dev/rework runner" (generic).

All other machinery (pin precedence, summary line, post-action wiring) is repo-agnostic and stays.

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + post-action contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite: 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```

### Thread 6 — `setup/dart.sh` line 437

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: v-prefixed `.dart-version` pin reports a false `match: no`**

`resolve_target` strips the muscle-memory `v` prefix (the `TARGET="${TARGET#v}"` rule, unit-tested: "a v-prefixed .dart-version token is stripped"), but `cmd_summary` compares the **raw** `repo_version_pin` token against the installed version. Verified live in a hermetic sandbox — `.dart-version` containing `v3.13.5` with the exact matching SDK 3.13.5 installed:

```bash
$ dart.sh plan   → requested=3.13.5  mode=version  source=version file   # install/cache-hit path: matches
$ dart.sh summary
toolchain: dart 3.13.5 (CI: v3.13.5, match: no)                            # summary: claims MISMATCH
```

The leg provably runs the pinned SDK, yet the machine-generated summary tells the reviewer (and the next agent leg, which reads this line to decide whether to trust its `dart format` verdict — the exact gh-1137 failure mode) that it does not. The `CI:` slot also displays the unprefixed-for-URLs `v3.13.5` token.

**Suggested fix**: derive the pin from what `resolve_target` already resolved instead of re-reading the file — e.g. when `SOURCE = "version file"` use `pin="$VERSION"; pin_kind="version"`, when `SOURCE = "quality workflow"` use the detected `det_sdk`/`det_channel` — so the summary and the install path can never drift (this duplication is the root cause). A test with `versionFile: 'v3.13.5\n'` + matching banner asserting `match: yes` would pin the behavior.

---

### Thread 7 — `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` line 72

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: script path is workingDir-prefixed AND run inside workingDirectory — double prefix silently no-ops the line on nested workingDir layouts**

`resolveDartScriptPath` returns `<workingDir>/setup/dart.sh` (needed: `file_read` resolves against the engine process cwd), but the same prefixed string is then used as the **command** executed with `workingDirectory: workingDir`. Command text in this codebase is workingDirectory-relative — every sibling caller pairs plain repo-relative commands with `workingDirectory` (`js/common/gitStaging.js` `git check-ignore …`, `js/common/pullRequest.js` `git rev-parse …`, and `runSetupCommands` in `js/common/setupCommands.js`, which is why the runners' own preamble is `bash agents/setup/dart.sh` per `README.md` §"dart toolchain", not `bash <workingDir>/agents/setup/dart.sh`).

So for any leg with a real nested `workingDir` (monorepo subdir layouts):

```text
file_read sees (process cwd):   <workingDir>/agents/setup/dart.sh  ✓ found
cli_execute_command runs:       cd <workingDir> && bash <workingDir>/agents/setup/dart.sh summary
                              → bash: <workingDir>/<workingDir>/agents/setup/dart.sh: No such file → exit 127
                              → caught, warn, line silently never appended
```

The feature's contract — "every leg summary carries the toolchain line" — silently fails precisely on the layouts the 3-candidate probe (`setup/`, `agents/`, `factory-agents/`) was written for. It works today only because all wired runners (`fa-story-dev`/`fa-rework`/`fa-bug-dev`) use `workingDir: "."`, where `./x` is cwd-invariant.

**Fix**: invoke the workingDir-relative fragment inside the workingDirectory — keep `resolveDartScriptPath` returning the prefixed path for `file_read`, but strip `workingDir + '/'` for the command (or have it return `{probePath, runPath}`). A regression test with a non-`.` workingDir asserting `command === 'bash setup/dart.sh summary' && workingDirectory === 'repo'` would lock the contract.

---

**dmtools-factory-bot** (2026-10-20):
💡 **SUGGESTION: the warning-line pickup is a hidden cross-file string contract**

`fetchToolchainLines` only rides the ⚠️ line along when it starts with `⚠️`, contains the exact substring `differ from CI`, and sits immediately after the `toolchain:` line — all mirroring `cmd_summary`'s wording in `setup/dart.sh`. # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ───────────────────────────────…
Now let me look at the test files: test_toolchainSummary.js, test_dartSetup.js, and the diffs on pushReworkChanges.js, developTicketAndCreatePR.js.

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
{"command":"sed -n 60,200p .github/workflows/quality.yml"}

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

## PR Description

Closes #1137

## Problem

A dev/rework agent that provisions its Dart SDK independently of the target repo ends up with an SDK that differs from the one the repo's CI pins. Dart's formatter and analyzer are version-sensitive: the agent then re-flows hundreds of files CI considers clean, calls CI's 3 changed files "clean", and — worst of all — **disputes a mechanical `dart_format` red**, loop-escalating over a fix that is purely mechanical. A mismatched SDK also poisons analyzer-based claims and any "format-clean" self-verification in the leg summary.

This is a **generic factory property, not a property of any one consumer repo**: every deployment whose runners build Dart projects needs the agent's toolchain to match the repo's CI pin.

### What changed
- `setup/dart.sh` precedence (gh-1137): explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; repos without `pubspec.yaml` skip the install entirely.
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)`; the append is a no-op on failure, non-Dart repos, and when the line is already present.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`).

### Review round 1 (fa-specific must not live in this repo) — to address in the rework leg

The dev/rework **runner configs** are per-deployment artifacts and belong in the consuming repo (or a deployment override), not committed here:

- `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json`, `.dmtools/runners/fa-rework.json` (added in this PR) — move out of dmtools-agents; the runner preamble should be generic: any Dart repo's runner opts into `bash setup/dart.sh` via its own config.
- The two UTs asserting the fa runner configs by name (`fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json customParams.setupCommands`) — replace with generic contracts: e.g. "if a runner config declares a dart preamble, it runs setup/dart.sh" + the setup/summary scripts' own unit tests (already 54+14 cases).
- The `setup/dart.sh` header comment referencing the fa dev/rework runner — reword to "the dev/rework runner" (generic).

All other machinery (pin precedence, summary line, post-action wiring) is repo-agnostic and stays.

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + post-action contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite: 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```

{
  "key": "pr-1138",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "Rework runner: use the target repo's CI Dart SDK (SDK mismatch made the agent dispute a mechanical dart_format red)",
    "description": "Closes #1137

## Problem

A dev/rework agent that provisions its Dart SDK independently of the target repo ends up with an SDK that differs from the one the repo's CI pins. Dart's formatter and analyzer are version-sensitive: the agent then re-flows hundreds of files CI considers clean, calls CI's 3 changed files "clean", and — worst of all — **disputes a mechanical `dart_format` red**, loop-escalating over a fix that is purely mechanical. A mismatched SDK also poisons analyzer-based claims and any "format-clean" self-verification in the leg summary.

This is a **generic factory property, not a property of any one consumer repo**: every deployment whose runners build Dart projects needs the agent's toolchain to match the repo's CI pin.

### What changed
- `setup/dart.sh` precedence (gh-1137): explicit value → `DART_VERSION` → repo `.dart-version` pin → `dart-lang/setup-dart` `sdk:`/`channel:` in the repo's workflows → stable **with a loud "may differ from CI" warning**; repos without `pubspec.yaml` skip the install entirely.
- New network-free `dart.sh summary` emits `toolchain: dart <version> (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)`; the append is a no-op on failure, non-Dart repos, and when the line is already present.
- `js/common/toolchainSummary.js` appends the line in both post actions (`developTicketAndCreatePR.js`, `pushReworkChanges.js`).

### Review round 1 (fa-specific must not live in this repo) — to address in the rework leg

The dev/rework **runner configs** are per-deployment artifacts and belong in the consuming repo (or a deployment override), not committed here:

- `.dmtools/runners/fa-story-dev.json`, `.dmtools/runners/fa-rework.json` (added in this PR) — move out of dmtools-agents; the runner preamble should be generic: any Dart repo's runner opts into `bash setup/dart.sh` via its own config.
- The two UTs asserting the fa runner configs by name (`fa-story-dev.json` / `fa-rework.json customParams.setupCommands`) — replace with generic contracts: e.g. "if a runner config declares a dart preamble, it runs setup/dart.sh" + the setup/summary scripts' own unit tests (already 54+14 cases).
- The `setup/dart.sh` header comment referencing the fa dev/rework runner — reword to "the dev/rework runner" (generic).

All other machinery (pin precedence, summary line, post-action wiring) is repo-agnostic and stays.

### How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_dartSetup.json          # 54 tests — pin precedence, warning, summary line (AC2/AC3)
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_toolchainSummary.json   # 14 tests — summary append + post-action contracts
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json                # full suite: 5499 passed / 0 failed
bash setup/dart.sh summary                            # live: n/a skip on non-Dart repos
```"
  }
}

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
